done_when: After the parent part is squash-merged and the default branch has moved, forge close on the stacked part replays only the part's own work, does not stop on the parent's record files, and goes on to the review; a new client repo and a repo adopted on an earlier release both get this

known.title: Preserve uncommitted work when rebase fails
Not done: Parent work picked up by a stacked part is still treated as its own
Retain the proof list when collapsing a replay

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 5
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - A coordinator closes a stacked part after its parent lands while the part’s checkout has uncommitted tracked edits.
Git refuses to start the rebase because the checkout is dirty. The new fallback treats that failure as a commit conflict, ignores the failed abort, and hard-resets to the default branch, permanently discarding the edits. Close does not check that the worktree is clean first; the worker can explicitly leave uncommitted changes with a warning at src/forge/worker.py:432.
Adds work: refuse non-conflict rebase failures before resetting; F 1 x H 1 = 1; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Preserve uncommitted work when rebase fails

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - Part B picks up an intermediate revision of parent A before A finishes review and is squash-merged.
The unmet item is: “After the parent part is squash-merged and the default branch has moved, forge close on the stacked part replays only the part's own work, does not stop on the parent's record files, and goes on to the review; a new client repo and a repo adopted on an earlier release both get this”.
New evidence beyond the ruling: if A changes a file after B starts, B picks up that change, and A reverts it before landing, the tree calculated at src/forge/close.py:719–726 treats A’s reverted edit as B’s work and can reintroduce it. Alternatively, if A updates the same review-record field again before landing, src/forge/close.py:727–730 can refuse on that parent record before the new fallback runs. B need not have edited either file.
findings.title: Not done: Parent work picked up by a stacked part is still treated as its own

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A user-facing stacked part has a proof list followed by the required final Functional check paragraph.
The fallback removes the worker’s commits, but src/forge/close.py:740–743 copies only the Functional check when it exists. The earlier Proof list is therefore absent from the replacement commit. src/forge/review.py:305–306 reads the list from the remaining history, so the subsequent review sees it as missing and can block with Gate: proof list even though the worker supplied it.
findings.title: Retain the proof list when collapsing a replay

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A story part picks up its parent’s later review records, then closes after the parent is squash-merged.
The named proof calls stacked(), which starts both items with forge fix start, as shown in tests/test_close_replays_followup_after_squash_merge.py:17–25 and tests/test_stacked_fixes_count_only_their_own_changes.py:36–39. It changes src/review_note.py rather than the parent’s .factory record and does not assert that review ran. Both new and previously adopted parameters can therefore pass if the story-part-specific path or the promised review is broken. The existing story-part tests do not exercise these later parent-review commits.
findings.title: Gate: stacked-part replay proof

why: A story part that was started on its parent part's unmerged branch cannot close after the parent is squash-merged: when the default branch has moved, close replays every commit since the part's recorded start, and that includes the parent's later review commits that the part picked up, so the replay conflicts in the parent's record file under .factory even though the file is the same as on the default branch (reported from client work)
